title: Expressions with set and put
subtitle: set off, set up, put up with, put your foot down
summary: Use the phrasal verbs and fixed expressions built on set and put, and swap them for more formal verbs in writing.

lesson.heading: Phrasal verbs with set
rows: reserve (money, time); also ignore, not think about (feelings)
begin a journey; also cause (an explosion, a wave of protest)
begin something with a particular aim in mind

lesson.heading: set in a story
lesson.text: Read how they work together. Since his daughter's birth, Robert had been putting money away for her wedding, and now he was on his way to meet her new fiance, Carl.

examples.text: Robert had been **setting aside** money for her wedding.
He and his wife were **setting off** to meet Carl.
Carl had **set out** several times to climb Mount Everest.
Now he was trying to **set up** a sports equipment business.
Robert was doing his best to **set aside** his negative feelings.

lesson.heading: Phrasal verbs with put 1
rows: present (a play); pretend to have (an accent)
lesson.note: Emma put her own name forward for election. She is very good at putting her ideas across, and she also has a talent for putting her opponents down.

lesson.heading: Phrasal verbs with put 2
rows: tidy things back where they belong
give accommodation to; display (a poster); raise (prices)
lesson.note: The play won't put staff out at all. / She would put up relatives coming from other towns. / The chairperson really put me off with his constant sniffing. / I don't know how they put up with the secretary's rudeness.

lesson.heading: Fixed expressions with set
rows: long to have or become something
decide on something you are aiming to do
discuss the important problems of the day
behave in a way others should copy

lesson.heading: Fixed expressions with put
rows: try to force them to do something
something arranged to give a false impression

lesson.text: Put off has two very different meanings: postpone the meeting, but also discourage a person. Only the object tells you which one it is.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its formal equivalent.

pairs.left: set off a wave of protests

exercises.prompt: Which noun does NOT normally follow put up?
exercises.explanation: You put in a comment, but you put up an umbrella, prices or a picture.

exercises.prompt: He's always so rude. What would you say to your friend?
options: I wouldn't put up with it if I were you.
I wouldn't put it off if I were you.
I wouldn't put it together if I were you.
I wouldn't put it forward if I were you.

exercises.prompt: This room is in a terrible mess. - Sorry, I haven't had time to put things ___ yet.
exercises.explanation: Put things away = tidy them back where they belong.

exercises.prompt: Any chance of a bed on your floor this weekend? - Yes, of course, I can put you ___.
exercises.explanation: Put someone up = give them accommodation.

exercises.prompt: Why have you suddenly lost interest in the project? - The cost of it all has put me ___.
exercises.explanation: Put someone off = distract or discourage them.

exercises.prompt: What is Adam planning to do after his business degree? - He is hoping to ___ a business of his own.
exercises.explanation: Set up a business = establish it.

exercises.prompt: Her aim is to become Prime Minister. - She has set her ___ on becoming Prime Minister.
exercises.explanation: Set your sights on / set your heart on = long to have or become something.

exercises.prompt: I find her terribly irritating. - She really puts my ___ up.
exercises.explanation: Put someone's back up = irritate them.

exercises.prompt: Please concentrate on the problem in hand. - Please put your ___ to the problem in hand.
exercises.explanation: Put your mind to something = direct all your thoughts towards it.

exercises.statement: She threw petrol on the rubbish and set fire to it.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Set fire to something = put a match to it.

exercises.statement: It's time the teacher set a stop to the noise.
exercises.explanation: It's time the teacher put a stop to the noise. Put an end / a stop to = cause something to stop.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order. (Be firm with him or there'll be trouble.)
exercises.answer: You really should put your foot down
exercises.explanation: Put your foot down = be firm about something.
